# Results — Study 871 (The Rank Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Hartzmark
(2015): investors disproportionately **sell the best- and worst-ranked positions** in their
portfolio, so the extreme-ranked names carry predictable selling pressure and should
**underperform the middle** of the ranking next period. Cross-sectional proxy: rank names by
trailing return, short both tails / long the middle, **controlling for the raw return level**.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `5384b8f7f128` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-42-day return**, ranked cross-sectionally; a name's **rank extremity** `|2u−1| ∈ [0,1]` (0 in the middle, 1 at either tail) is the signal, known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day **long the middle 40%** of the ranking, **short both 20% tails** (rank-1 winners + rank-N losers), equal weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Level control | the both-tails short is *approximately* level-neutral by construction (a big winner + a big loser average toward the middle); a **level-controlled** cut residualises the forward return on a quadratic in the standardised trailing-return level, then re-measures the middle-minus-extremes spread |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short (extremes) book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled middle-vs-extremes books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Hartzmark's
rank effect is a **retail-portfolio, individual-position** phenomenon (salience of *your own*
holdings' extremes); a fixed 50-mega-cap cross-section is only a proxy, and exactly the kind of
liquid tape where any residual rank-position mispricing should be arbitraged away.

## The headline — long-middle / short-extremes rank-extremity spread

Daily equal-weight middle-40% minus both-20%-tails spread (n = **4,104** days, ~50 names/day):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long middle − short extremes)** | **−1.65 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−1.86** |
| one-sample *t* | −1.88 |
| middle book / extremes book | +6.71 bps / +8.36 bps (Welch *t* = −0.64) |
| level neutrality (mean trailing ret) | middle +2.47% vs extremes +3.87% |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.46 |

The claim predicts a **positive** spread — the salient extremes should *under*-earn the middle.
On this mega-cap tape the spread is **−1.65 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−1.86**): if anything the
extreme-ranked names *out*-earned the middle, and the effect is **not significant** (|t| < 2).
The claimed rank-extremity underperformance is absent — the sign is even backwards.

## Controlling for the raw return level — the effect vanishes entirely

The whole point of the rank effect is that it is about **rank position**, not the return level.
Residualise each day's forward return on a quadratic in the standardised trailing-return level
(removing *any* smooth momentum / reversal curve), then re-measure the middle-minus-extremes
spread:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **level-controlled spread** | **+0.11 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+0.18** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.17 |

Once the raw return level is controlled for, the spread collapses to a **flat zero** (+0.11
bps/day, *t* = +0.18). The small raw −1.65 bps is entirely a level (momentum) artefact of the
tails, not a rank-position effect. There is **no** rank-extremity signal here.

## Placebo — is the (already wrong-signed) relation even a real alignment?

Keep the rank-extremity sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−1.65 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.036 bps (0.789) |
| position of observed | ≈ **2.14σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 0.981) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −1.65 bps sits ~2σ into the **left** tail —
the opposite direction to the claim, and the level-controlled cut shows even that is a level
artefact, not a rank-position effect.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,970) | −0.58 bps | **−0.50** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −2.63 bps | **−1.99** |

The early era is a flat nothing; the late era is a marginal wrong-signed −1.99. The effect is
neither stable nor claim-signed — no robust rank-extremity underperformance in either half.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −1.65 bps | 2.14 bps | **−3.79 bps** | −4.31 | −1.07 | −9.5%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −1.65 bps | 10.14 bps | **−11.79 bps** | −13.42 | −3.32 | −29.7%/yr |

The specified book (long middle / short extremes) loses money **gross** (the spread is negative
for the claimed direction) and is buried by friction net. Even the data-mined sign-flip earns
only +1.65 bps/day gross, which the 2.14 bps/day round-trip at a mere 1 bp one-way already eats.
**Mirage** in either direction.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel where names at an **extreme trailing-return rank** carry a forward
penalty proportional to their rank extremity (`edge > 0`); null at `edge = 0`. No network.

| world | level-controlled spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.24** (sd 0.96), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0016`, seed 871) | raw *t* = **+4.14**, level-controlled *t* = **+2.33** |

The detector recovers a *planted* rank-extremity relation cleanly — both raw and after
controlling for the level — and stays silent on the null. So the flat real-tape result is a
genuine absence, not a broken sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Hartzmark's rank effect does **not** show up as cross-sectional return
  predictability on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-middle / short-extremes spread is
  **−1.65 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−1.86**) — *wrong-signed* (extremes if anything out-earned) and
  **insignificant**; and once you **control for the raw return level** — the whole point of the
  test — it collapses to **+0.11 bps/day** (*t* = +0.18), a flat zero. Not robust across eras
  (*t* = −0.50 / −1.99). The 20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* relation cleanly, so
  this is a real absence. The rank effect is a retail-position, behavioural-trading phenomenon
  that leaves no tradable footprint in this liquid cross-section.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The specified book loses money gross and net (−3.79 bps/day at 1 bp,
  −11.79 at 5 bps); even the data-mined sign-flip is eaten by the round-trip friction at 1 bp.
